meter.title: The meter after the click
meter.caption: A click should light every tone a little. Right after it, the meter showed one thin spike, at the one tone the notch removes.

split-zero.title: Sample 0 is the click plus the ring
split-zero.caption: The first output sample is two things added: the click passing straight through and the very start of the ring. After that, only the ring is left.

click-ring.title: One click, and the notch rings
click-ring.caption: After the click the output never quite stops: up, nothing, down, nothing, at 2,000 Hz, each swing 0.9 of the one before per sample.

spiral.title: A pole pair in time is a spiral
spiral.caption: The turn per sample is the ring’s pitch, the shrink per sample is its decay. After one sample the dot sits exactly on the pole.

decay-time.title: Decay time: down to 1%
decay-time.caption: The decay time is how long the ring takes to fall to 1% of where it started. At radius 0.9 that is 43.7 samples, 5.5 ms.

pole-gaps.title: Halve the gap, double the ring
pole-gaps.caption: Each time the pole halves its gap to the circle, its ring lasts twice as long.

whine-on.title: The whine switching on rings too
whine-on.caption: From n = 2 on the zero pair cancels the whine exactly. The first sample had nothing to cancel against, and the feedback carries it on as a fading ring.

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth: the notch’s width at 71%
bandwidth.caption: The bandwidth is the distance between the two tones where the notch passes 71%. Poles closer to the circle make it narrower.

trade-off.title: Every notch sits on one curve
trade-off.caption: Pick a pole radius and you pick a point on this curve. A short ring means a wide notch, a narrow notch means a long ring.

half-turn.title: Two samples back: half a turn, a little farther out
half-turn.caption: Two samples is half a turn, which flips the shadow’s sign, and two shrinks of 0.9, which is 0.81. Together: × −0.81, exactly the feedback rule.

click-minus-ring.title: The notch is a click minus a ring
click-minus-ring.caption: A click is every tone at once. Take away the ring, a narrow peak at 2,000 Hz, and what is left is the notch.

triangle.title: Near the top, a right triangle
triangle.caption: Near the whine only two distances matter: to the top zero, about a, and to the top pole, the triangle’s long side.

drift.title: Telling close tones apart takes time
drift.caption: Two tones 50 Hz apart look alike at first. Only after 10 ms are they half a cycle apart.

ninety.title: Where the notch gets back to 90%
ninety.caption: For this notch a tone gets back to 90% about one bandwidth away from the whine.

radius-strip.title: The window of radii
radius-strip.caption: The first request and the second never meet. The first and the third overlap in a short window.
